chunks: I said to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: “The people of Makkah perform the prayer in full at ‘Arafāt.” So he said: “Woe to them, or alas for them! And what journey is more arduous than it? It is not to be performed in full.”

key_terms.لَا يُتَمُّ: it is not to be performed in full
key_terms.يُتِمُّونَ: they perform in full, without shortening

ai.seo_question: Should the people of Makkah shorten or complete their prayer at ‘Arafāt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the prayer at ‘Arafāt, indicating that travelers, including the people of Makkah in this context, should not perform the prayer in full there. The Imam عليه السلام strongly emphasizes that this journey is a true travel situation requiring the shortened prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "The people of Mecca pray the full (four-unit) prayer at Arafat."
Imam (as) said: "Woe to them, or alas for them! What journey is more arduous than this? It should not be performed in full (but shortened to two units)."
